chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Ray Charles band lineup and gospel style
summary: Smith lists Fathead Newman, Leroy Cooper, Clint Smith, his bassist brother and drummers, and says Ray started gospel-flavored music in the region.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I guess so. I don't know. He was staying in one place and I was in another. All the boys were down there where I
Buster Smith - 189
was. They always stayed around where I was anyhow, mostly all of them...
Who was in the band? Fathead Newman?
Fathead. Leroy Cooper.
Who was the trumpet player?
Clint Smith. And Biscuit; I think Biscuit was in there, a trumpet player. A boy called Biscuit. He was a good trumpet player. Read good and everything.
And the rhythm section was Ray on piano...
Yeah, Ray on piano and I think... Let me see. I had my brother on bass. I think my brother was on bass...
And the drummer?
And the drummer was S.D. Young a while, and then sometimes I used Robert Cobbs who lives down in Waxahachie.
Was Ray into his Gospel thing by then?
His what?
Was he doing that sort of Gospel-influenced music at that time?
Yeah.
Even that early?
Yeah. Mmm-hmm.
Was he the first person to really do that?
No. Not that I know of. I heard several cats back down in Florida, back down that way, in Alabama and all
Buster Smith - 190

through there, who had that kind of style. Little Richard was one of them. He stopped and went to preaching. But he was one of them. But Ray, mostly he was a... He's the one who started that around this part of the country. Especially here in Dallas and back out West here -- West Texas.
